hypothesis: If Q90 is the common dominant signed local shape-bias injector, the dominant bias is the same non-well-balanced layer-mean hydraulic-gradient defect already exposed by hydrostatic-preservation analysis, and can be reduced by subtracting the C0 Q90 flux of the hydrostatic equilibrium state at the same prescribed H.

execution_condition.rule: For all six dynamic width/history cases, Q90 must rank first by cumulative_injection_shape_rms_theta_at_final_geometry on both the 0.00005-day primary and 0.000025-day cross routes.
execution_condition.hold_role: WT_HOLD is a supporting equilibrium control but is not sufficient to authorize C4A.
execution_condition.if_false: Do not execute universal Q90 correction. Close as REGIME_SPECIFIC_LOCAL_BIAS and design a separate diagnostic from frozen C3 evidence.

counterfactual.model_change_scope: teacher-forced diagnostic only; replace Q90 closure and no other channel
counterfactual.equilibrium_Q90: evaluate the identical C0 q90 formula on exact hydrostatic layer-mean storages for the fixed 80-90 cm layer and moving bulk 90..H-d at the same prescribed H and terminal width d
counterfactual.exact_property: At an exactly hydrostatic projected state, corrected Q90 is zero up to numerical quadrature/root precision.

stage_A_teacher_forced_test.start_state: exact A2 Reference projection at every interval
compare: original C0 teacher local state injection
primary_metrics: Q90 signed and absolute integrated bias
cumulative local-bias storage vector shape norm
q_i and q_H local errors as non-target channels

progression_rule.teacher_support_required: Q90_WB must exactly pass the hydrostatic HOLD control and reduce the mass-neutral local shape-injection RMS in every six dynamic case on both time-step routes without increasing absolute integrated qH bias or violating any hard gate.
progression_rule.if_supported: A later separately preregistered C4B may test free propagated dynamics.
progression_rule.if_not_supported: Do not propagate Q90_WB; retain bias localization and investigate regime-dependent or multi-channel closure.
